lines.text: Four years ago, this was what AI video looked like.
This is what four years did.
In 2022, research labs showed that plain words could become moving pictures.
But clips lasted a few seconds, and early animation drew every frame on its own.
In 2023, Runway's Gen-2 put text-to-video into public hands.
Then, in February 2024, OpenAI previewed Sora, promising up to a minute of video.
Suddenly, a subject could hold together across a shot. It reset expectations.
Then the race began. In June 2024 alone, Kling, Luma and Runway all showed new models.
By December, Sora was public, and Google's Veo 2 arrived a week later.
In May 2025, Veo 3 generated sound along with the picture.
By September 2026, developers announce thirty-second clips, native 4K, and generated sound.
Light behaves. Water moves. Shots hold together for seconds, not frames.
Even Sora, the 2024 sensation, was shut down this year.
Now the frame itself is changing. Genie 3 builds worlds you can steer, in real time.
Motion was the miracle. Now it's the baseline.
From melting pixels... to moving worlds.
